_comment: Host attribution for competitor Juliet runs, kept OUTSIDE the run JSONs.
bench/competitors.py has never recorded a hostname, so the run blobs cannot
say where they executed. They are the archival record of what the tool
captured and are deliberately not retro-edited; this file carries what was
established afterwards, with the source of that knowledge stated per entry.
Wall clock is the only figure in a run that is hardware-dependent, and the
April and September sets did NOT run on comparable machines -- see the
hosts below. Durations must not be compared across a host boundary.
bench/competitor_csv.py reads this to fill the hostname and hostname_source
columns. `runner` there would mean the run recorded it itself; every entry
here is `attributed`. Delete an entry once the run JSON carries its own.

r720.description: Dell PowerEdge R720, ~2012-era Xeon. Roughly ten years older than dev-921 and materially slower per core.

dev-921.description: 12th Gen Intel Core i5-12400, 6 cores / 12 threads, 31 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.
